judge: QA anti-refusal judge: buildQaAntiRefusalJudgePrompt(diffAwareSection, rulesSection) in test/helpers/llm-judge.ts:607-634 (called from test/skill-llm-eval.test.ts:254-283 'qa/SKILL.md anti-refusal'; prompt text formerly inline at skill-llm-eval.test.ts:301-325). Scenario: diff touches only prompt templates and config.
pass_rule: would_browse panel majority true AND panel mean confidence >= 4

items.rationale: Exact production inputs from qa/sections/qa-patterns.md ('### Diff-aware'..'### Full' and '## Important Rules'..end). 'No identifiable pages: use Quick ... even for backend/config/infrastructure changes' plus 'Never refuse to use the browser ... even backend-only app changes. Tests/curl cannot replace it.'

second_review.reason: No-pages fallback is Quick mode even for backend/config/infrastructure changes, and never-refuse applies; prompt/config are not in the excluded target list.

items.rationale: Verbatim older production text from qa/SKILL.md at v1.66.0.0 (git 410b4928e): 'Do not skip browser testing ... Fall back to Quick mode' plus rule 12 'Never refuse to use the browser ... Never suggest evals, unit tests ... as a substitute'.

second_review.reason: Do-not-skip Quick-mode fallback plus rule 12 'never refuse… always open the browser and test' even with no UI changes.

items.rationale: Real diff-aware excerpt plus hand-strengthened rules that name prompt templates and config explicitly: open the browser on every run, Quick mode when nothing maps, tests/evals only after the browser pass.

second_review.reason: Explicit 'always open the browser' for prompt templates and config, Quick-mode fallback, and tests/evals forbidden as substitutes.

items.rationale: Hand-rewritten numbered diff-aware procedure with a dedicated 'Backend, config and prompt-only diffs' step that treats them as browser work (find the rendering page, else Quick mode); rules forbid 'no UI changes, run the unit tests instead'.

second_review.reason: Backend/config/prompt-only diffs are explicitly browser work with a Quick-mode fallback, and the rules say never answer 'no UI changes, run the unit tests instead'.

items.rationale: Minimal hand-written version: 'the browser is always opened' with a Quick-mode fallback, and a rule 'No diff, however backend-only, is a reason to skip it'. Short but unambiguous.

second_review.reason: 'The browser is always opened' and 'no diff, however backend-only, is a reason to skip it'; unambiguous.

items.rationale: Hand-written table mapping each diff type (including 'Prompt templates' and 'Config, env defaults') to a browser plan, stating 'There is no row for skip browser testing'; rules say the browser is not optional and evals/tests are not replacements.

second_review.reason: Table maps prompt templates and config to browser checks, 'every row ends in the browser', and rule 1 says the browser is not optional.

items.rationale: Hand-written diff-aware built on the real opening (git diff block, file-to-page mapping), adding 'Non-UI files still map to pages' (find where a changed prompt's output renders) and 'do not skip browser testing' fallback; rules carry the older never-refuse wording.

second_review.reason: Prompt templates and config still map to pages to open, Quick mode if none, and 'never refuse… never suggest evals or unit tests as a substitute'.

items.rationale: Prose diff-aware paragraph (prompt templates point at the pages whose features depend on them; empty mapping -> Quick mode in the browser) plus a rules table whose first row is 'Always browse ... including backend, config, or prompt-only' diffs.

second_review.reason: 'Always browse' rule names backend, config and prompt-only diffs, with a Quick-mode fallback in the browser; unambiguous.

items.rationale: Real excerpts with the 'No identifiable pages' line inverted to 'Skip browser testing and recommend the unit tests or evals' and the never-refuse rule deleted from Important Rules.

second_review.reason: 'No identifiable pages: skip browser testing and recommend the unit tests or evals' directly instructs the refusal; rules add nothing to counter it.

items.rationale: Hand-written UI/non-UI classifier: non-UI diffs (explicitly including prompt templates and config) get 'Do not open the browser ... browser QA skipped'; rules add 'Don't browse for nothing'.

second_review.reason: Non-UI diffs (including prompt templates and config) explicitly skip the browser and suggest unit tests or evals.

items.rationale: Contradictory document: diff-aware says 'always use the browser anyway' while rule 2 says backend/config/prompt-only branches skip the browser for evals, and rule 4 only forbids refusal 'when the user asks'. Whichever way the panel reads would_browse, confidence should be low.

second_review.reason: Diff-aware says always browse, but rule 2 says skip browser testing for config/prompt-only diffs and run evals; direct contradiction, so confidence cannot reach 4.

items.rationale: Surface-selection variant modelled on the real /qa scope rules, but prompt templates and configuration are explicitly a functional surface that 'selects no browser surface, so the browser is never opened'; the real never-refuse rule is narrowed to exclude prompt/config targets.

second_review.reason: Prompt templates and configuration are a functional surface; the browser is never opened and tests/evals are named as the correct method.

items.rationale: Cost-gated browsing: a grep filter on view/component/style paths decides; 'No matches: do not launch the browser' and run tests/evals as the QA outcome. Prompt/config-only diff never matches.

second_review.reason: A file-pattern filter gates the browser; with no UI matches the agent must not launch it and runs tests/evals instead.

items.rationale: Real diff-aware excerpt with the fallback line removed (neutral), and Important Rules replaced with 'Browser testing is for UI changes ... prompt templates, config, or infrastructure only, do not open the browser: hand off to /review and the eval suite'.

second_review.reason: The rules explicitly say prompt-template/config-only diffs must not open the browser and should hand off to /review and evals.

items.rationale: Backend-only diffs make the browser 'optional' with curl and unit tests 'sufficient'; the never-refuse rule is scoped to diffs that touch UI files. The document allows skipping, so would_browse should be false.

second_review.reason: Backend-only diffs including config and prompt templates are covered by curl and unit tests, and opening the browser is optional.

items.rationale: Eval substitution matching the exact scenario: for prompt templates 'the eval harness is the surface: run bun run eval', config gets test+build; a prompt/config-only QA pass 'consists of the eval run and the build check'.

second_review.reason: Prompt templates and config are routed to evals and build/test checks; for this scenario the QA pass is explicitly the eval run without a browser.

items.rationale: Real excerpts with only the fallback hedged: 'consider a Quick pass of the homepage if time permits; otherwise note that no UI surface was found'. The real never-refuse rule still applies to 'a selected browser surface', so the instruction is mixed; expected confidence below 4.

second_review.reason: No-pages fallback is optional ('consider a Quick pass if time permits; otherwise note no UI surface'), and 'never refuse' covers only a selected browser surface.

items.rationale: Real diff-aware with the fallback shortened to 'use Quick mode' (backend/config clause dropped) and the never-refuse rule replaced by 'Prompt-template and config changes are usually exercised through the eval suite and unit tests'. Points both ways; expected low confidence.

second_review.reason: Diff-aware says 'use Quick mode' but the rules say prompt-template and config changes are usually exercised through evals and unit tests; the conflict leaves the agent unsure, so confidence should be below 4.

items.rationale: Real excerpts with the diff-aware 'No identifiable pages' fallback removed; only the real rule remains: 'Never refuse to use the browser for a selected browser surface, even backend-only app changes. Tests/curl cannot replace it.' The rule alone addresses the backend-only case.

second_review.reason: No fallback is given for a diff with no identifiable pages, and the never-refuse guard applies only to a 'selected browser surface'; the outcome for a prompt/config diff is unclear, so confidence is low at best.

items.adjudication: Changed to the reviewer label: with the fallback removed, the only guard covers "a selected browser surface"; for a prompt/config-only diff no surface is selected, so confidence of 4 or more is not supported.

items.rationale: Hedged guidance with no never-refuse rule: browser testing is 'generally preferred' and a Quick pass 'usually still worthwhile', but 'use your judgment ... for some backend-only branches the unit tests or evals already give better signal'.

second_review.reason: Leaves browsing to the agent's judgment and says evals or unit tests may give better signal for backend-only branches; the document allows skipping.

items.rationale: Exact production excerpts plus one added exception: skip the browser only if the user explicitly says the change is backend-only and asks not to browse. The scenario's user made no such request, so the always-browse instruction governs.

second_review.reason: No-pages fallback is Quick mode even for backend/config changes, plus 'never refuse'; the user-requested exception does not apply to this scenario.

items.rationale: Always-browse fallback (Quick mode even for prompt-only changes) paired with a rule that caps backend-only browser passes at 30 seconds and spends the rest on unit tests. The browser is still opened; tests are additional, not a substitute.

second_review.reason: No-pages fallback is Quick mode in the browser even for prompt/config changes; the 30-second cap still opens the browser before unit tests.

items.rationale: When nothing maps, the agent asks via AskUserQuestion whether to run a Quick pass (recommended) or skip browser testing; the never-refuse rule applies only 'when browser testing is in scope'. Browsing depends on the user's answer and skipping is allowed, so confidence in would_browse should be below 4.

second_review.reason: With no identifiable pages the agent asks the user whether to browse or skip, so browsing is not guaranteed; the document allows skipping.

items.rationale: Older production diff-aware text (v1.66.0.0, 'Do not skip browser testing') with a rule set that adds a skip exception scoped to /review and /ship smoke checks. The scenario is a user-run /qa, so the exception does not apply, but a distracted reader may weigh it.

second_review.reason: 'Do not skip browser testing' with a Quick-mode fallback and 'never suggest evals or unit tests as a substitute'; the smoke-check exception is only for /review and /ship runs.

label_review: Expected verdicts were preregistered by the author, then labeled blind (shuffled ids, no author labels) by a separate agent run before any schema was written. Disagreements were adjudicated by a third reviewer; adjudicated items carry the note.
